text:
jon (support): FYI getting a flood of customer reports — lots of 5xx / timeouts on hosted API endpoints, started ~09:20 UTC. Opening a war-room thread. :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: WAR ROOM created for thread 1872345678 — channel #incidents — severity: high — links: https://runbook.internal/hosted-5xx
asha (oncall): I can join in 2 mins. First glance — dashboards show spike in edge 502s and gateway 504s, error-rate up 12x for v1/generate.
maria (eng-runtime): Noted. Any common pattern? specific model or route?
jon (support): Most reports reference /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream. A couple mention timeouts when using streaming responses.
leo (infra): Regions: us-east-1 and eu-west-1 primarily. Host-level errors on the gateway layer, but need to confirm if backend model pods are overloaded or the LB is dropping connections.
nash (ops-runner): forwarding traces from one complaining customer: trace id 0a3f3c. Logs show repeated `upstream prematurely closed connection` from envoy.
maria (eng-runtime): envoy upstream closed often indicates backend instance OOM or process crash. Can we get a tail of runtime logs from a failing replica?
leo (infra): pulling pods now. Command I ran: ```kubectl -n hosted-prod logs -l app=runtime -c runtime --since=5m | grep ERROR | tail -n 40``` got a bunch of `killed by OOM` and `failed to allocate tensor buffer` lines.
jon (support): So this is capacity-related? several customers also reported concurrent large-context requests.
nash (ops-runner): Repro steps for us: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"<~20k tokens prompt>"}'``` — on repro I saw `504 Gateway Time-out`.
maria (eng-runtime): Good repro. For immediate mitigation I recommend routing large-context requests to a slower-but-more-stable variant and enabling prefix cache for high-frequency prefixes. Can we push a traffic split?
nash (ops-runner): We can update routing rules in kong for hosted to send traffic to fallback pool: ```PATCH /configs/routes/hosted -> set weight: primary=60 fallback=40``` - prepping change.
leo (infra): Before traffic split, we should scale up runtime pods for short window. K8s HPA is reactive; I'm manually scaling deployment to +30% for the runtime group handling eu-west-1. ```kubectl -n hosted-prod scale deployment runtime-eu --replicas=26```
nash (ops-runner): Done for eu-west-1. us-east-1 scaling now.
nash (ops-runner): Also temporarily bumped gateway timeouts to 90s to reduce premature closes. ```envoy.timeout.upstream: 90s```
nash (ops-runner): Applying routing split now.
maria (eng-runtime): Monitoring KV cache / prefix cache hit rates. If prefix cache misses are high for these big prompts we won't see much improvement.
nash (ops-runner): After split + scale, 5xx rate dropped ~70% in eu-west-1 within 6m. us-east still noisy.
jon (support): Customers on support thread reporting fewer errors — leaving note to update them in 15. :white_check_mark:
nash (ops-runner): Found one runtime shard with frequent `OOM` on host i-0f9a3 — kernel OOM killer logs show multiple killed `runtime-worker` processes. Investigating instance health (maybe degraded NVMe).
leo (infra): Taking that host out of rotation. ```gcloud compute instances suspend i-0f9a3``` then cordon node from k8s.
nash (ops-runner): Node cordoned and replaced, pods rescheduled.
maria (eng-runtime): Looking at the model backend: one model variant (gptx-large-q4) had a regression in memory usage introduced in last deploy (rev 2026.11.2). Can we rollback that variant?
nash (ops-runner): Rolling back model variant to 2026.10.9 for gptx-large-q4 in eu-west-1. ```POST /admin/models/rollout rollback=2026.10.9 model=gptx-large-q4```
nash (ops-runner): Rollback done.
maria (eng-runtime): After rollback, memory pressure normalized on those replicas, OOM events stopped. 5xx down to near baseline in eu-west-1. us-east-1 completed scale + drain; errors there also falling.
nash (ops-runner): Patching gateway routing and reverting timeout bump to baseline now that backend is stable.
jon (support): Quick customer update: "We're seeing improved responses — thanks for the quick fix". closing some high-touch tickets.
nash (ops-runner): Noted one oddity: billing-bot flagged a set of customers with repeated retries during the incident causing >2x token usage spike. Could be billing noise. billing-bot, any details?
billing-bot: Alert: Customers CUST-998, CUST-1021 saw anomalous retry loops between 09:22-09:30 UTC resulting in extra generated tokens; we flagged billing protection and paused auto-invoice for those accounts. Full CSV attached to ops ticket #BILL-342.
jon (support): We'll follow up with customers re credits. Action item: Support to issue goodwill credits for impacted windows. Assigning: jon -> Due EOD.
maria (eng-runtime): Postmortem action items I want captured: 1) Add memory regression detection to pre-deploy smoke tests for model variants (owner: maria, due: 2026-04-02). 2) Improve autoscale headroom for large-context workloads (owner: leo, due: 2026-03-30). 3) Router-level knob to automatically divert heavy-context requests to fallback variants (owner: ashish, due: 2026-03-25).
nash (ops-runner): I'll add an alert to detect upstream OOM patterns earlier and automatically cordon node if repeated `runtime-worker` OOMKill in 5m (owner: nash/ops, due: 2026-03-20).
leo (infra): Also adding disk health checks to instance provisioning; possibly a flaky NVMe caused extra memory pressure (owner: leo, due: 2026-03-28).
nash (ops-runner): Temporary mitigations summary: scaled +30% runtime, rolled back variant 2026.11.2->2026.10.9, traffic split to fallback, bumped timeouts briefly, cordoned bad node, paused billing auto-invoices for affected customers.
jon (support): Running list of tickets to close and credits to issue. I'll attach timeline to each customer ticket.
maria (eng-runtime): For the postmortem doc: I'll draft root cause as "memory regression in model variant plus insufficient autoscale headroom for large-context requests leading to OOMs and upstream closes". Will include telemetry graphs and traces.
nash (ops-runner): One lingering item — we saw intermittent 401s for one OAuth token issuer around 09:21 which caused some retries; not primary cause of 5xx but will investigate auth cache TTLs. Assigning to ashish.
nash (ops-runner): Repro bundle (traces, logs, sample request) uploaded to /shared/incidents/1872345678/repro.zip
nash (ops-runner): Closing war-room thread for now — services stabilized across regions, continuing postmortem. :white_check_mark:
maria (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone — will follow up with postmortem doc and action items.
jon (support): Thanks team. I'll DM customers and attach status update.
nash (ops-runner): Postmortem follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC — invite sent to eng-runtime, infra, support, billing.
